question.text: What is 'pin risk' at option expiry?

answer.text: The risk that the underlying closes very near the option strike price at expiry, creating uncertainty about whether the option will be exercised — this is particularly problematic for option sellers who don't know their assignment status until after market close
The risk of being locked into a position that cannot be closed
The risk associated with entering a Personal Identification Number (PIN) for trading
The risk that the option premium falls to exactly zero before expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: Pin risk arises when, at expiry, the underlying settles very close to an option strike (e.g., NIFTY at 24,995 with a 25,000 strike). For short option positions, it is uncertain whether the option will finish in-the-money and be assigned, leaving the seller exposed to overnight gap risk because their final assignment status (and any resulting delivery/cash obligation) is not confirmed until after the official settlement price is determined. The Trap: Pin risk is specifically about expiry-day uncertainty over assignment, not about being unable to close a position, security credentials/PINs, or premiums falling to zero. Those options describe different concepts and do not capture the assignment-uncertainty mechanism that defines pin risk. Note: The specific term "pin risk" was not located in the cited Series VIII workbook pages (p.33 and p.157-p.159). The explanation above is framed using general industry knowledge about equity derivative expiry mechanics rather than as a citation from the workbook.
